metadata.summary: Harry Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, which could be one of the tightest results in recent history.
metadata.content: Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in race for men's award - stats and pundits' opinions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in race for men's award - stats and pundits' opinions Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe battling for 2026 men's Ballon d'Or on Monday; Kane odds-on favourite to become first Englishman to win the award in 25 years; Lamine Yamal, 19, aiming to become youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher backing Kane to win By Declan Olley & Adam Smith Monday 26 October 2026 07:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at who Sky Sports pundits and journalists are backing to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or Harry Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, which could be one of the tightest results in recent history. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years. messages.text: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit

metadata.summary: Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.
metadata.content: European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit Luke Littler suffered a quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajski, extending his wait for his elusive ranked TV title; Ross Smith beat Martin Schindler in the European Championship final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 25 October 2026 23:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the winning moment from Ross Smith's European Championship success, where he closed out an 11-8 victory over Martin Schindler. (Credit: ITV) Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund. The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen. Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw. messages.text: Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for world title

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.
metadata.content: United States GP: Kimi Antonelli wins Austin race to move to brink of F1 world title after dominant drive | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: Kimi Antonelli wins Austin race to move to brink of F1 world title after dominant drive Kimi Antonelli delivers emphatic victory in Austin to move a maximum of two points away from clinching 2026's Drivers' Championship; Antonelli only needs a ninth-place finish next Sunday in Mexico to be sure; Charles Leclerc's late surge secures second place in race from Max Verstappen Sunday 25 October 2026 23:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix. Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower. And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention. messages.text: How Antonelli can win world title at Mexico City GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday How can Kimi Antonelli become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history this Sunday at the Mexico City Grand Prix? Watch every session of the Mexico City GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 26 October 2026 06:22, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City. Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin to move 123 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate and nearest challenger George Russell, and 124 points ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris were officially knocked out of championship contention, leaving Russell and Hamilton as the only drivers who can technically prevent Antonelli from becoming the sport's youngest ever world champion at 20 years old. metadata.summary: England head coach Stuart Barrow insists his side remain positive of reaching the Women's Rugby League World Cup semi-finals, despite being 'blown away' in a 78-0 drubbing by Australia on Saturday.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England switch focus to winner-takes-all clash with Samoa after being 'blown away' by Australia | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England switch focus to winner-takes-all clash with Samoa after being 'blown away' by Australia England need to beat Samoa in their final group game to qualify for the Women's Rugby League World Cup semi-finals; England thrashed Wales in their tournament opener before losing 78-0 to Australia on Saturday Monday 26 October 2026 07:12, UK Image: England need to beat Samoa on Friday to reach the Rugby League Women's World Cup semi-finals England head coach Stuart Barrow insists his side remain positive of reaching the Women's Rugby League World Cup semi-finals, despite being 'blown away' in a 78-0 drubbing by Australia on Saturday. Nineteen months on from a humbling 90-4 loss to Australia in Las Vegas, England suffered another heavy defeat against the same opposition after the Jillaroos ran in 15 tries during a one-sided contest. England now travel from Perth to Wollongong for Friday's winner-takes-all clash with Samoa (6.45am GMT), where a victory is required to finish second in Group A and reach the knockout stages.
